question.leadin: Ozan Kilinc ("KILL-inch") was jailed by a court in this country for publishing articles sympathetic to a banned party.
question.text: Name this country, where insulting the country or the government is illegal under Article 301.
question.clue: This country was permitted to remilitarize a waterway by the Montreaux Convention.

swap.leadin: The Golden Horn cuts into this city and was once spanned by a large chain to prevent enemy ships from getting in.
swap.text: Name this Turkish city that was previously named Byzantium and Constantinople.
swap.clue: Cannons designed by the Hungarian engineer Orban were used to breach this city's Theodosian Walls.

question.leadin: A huge amount of impressive building projects were designed by this ruler's architect, Sinan.
question.text: Name this son of Selim the Grim, who won the Battle of Mohacs [Moe-HOTCH] but was less successful in conquering Malta and also led an unsuccessful siege of Vienna.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [or Suleiman the Lawgiver or Suleiman I; prompt on “Suleiman”]
question.clue: A principle known as the "circle of justice" guided the legal kanuns which he set up, and he supported the ascension of John Zapolya following one of his military victories.

swap.text: In the 1910s and 20s, the Young Turks perpetrated a genocide on this ethnic group, in which the Ottoman Empire forced this group from their homeland. The modern Turkish government refuses to identify the event as a genocide.
swap.answerHtml: Armenians (accept Armenian genocide or Armenian Holocaust, but do not prompt on Holocaust)
swap.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

question.text: This period of modernization, especially of the millet system, ended when Abdulhamid issued the First Ottoman Constitution.
question.clue: The Young Turk Revolution established the Ottoman Empire's second constitutional era; the first constitution put an end to this period of moderate reform that lasted from the 1839 Edict of Gulhane (gool-HAH-neh) to 1876.

swap.leadin: The path to becoming one of these people involved "scouting" in the devshirme system.
swap.text: Name these boy soldiers from the Balkans who were gathered by the Ottoman empire to fight in the military. They usually specialized in firearms.
swap.clue: When these people were eliminated, the closely-associated sect of Bektashi Sufism was banned.

question.text: Forces from New Zealand fought alongside those of Australia as part of the "Anzacs" during this disastrous 1916 British campaign in modern-day Turkey in World War I.
question.clue: This campaign included a disastrous attempt to divert attention from Suvla Bay during the August Offensive by having troops charge the Nek.

swap.leadin: Raphael Lemkin coined a term that was first used to describe this event.
swap.text: Name this event that was begun by mass deportations authorized by the Tehcir Law. One country's Article 301 prohibits discussing this event.
swap.clue: Henry Morgenthau Sr. wrote a firsthand account of this event, which began on "Red Sunday" with a deportation of intellectuals.

question.leadin: He died at the siege of Szigetvar after resuming warfare in Hungary in 1566.
question.text: Name this Ottoman sultan, the son of Selim the Grim, who defeated the aforementioned Hungarians at the great battle of Mohacs forty years earlier.
question.clue: This ruler expelled the Knights Hospitalers from Rhodes after conquering Belgrade, although the same group would defeat him at Malta later on.

swap.leadin: Shortly after his greatest victory, this ruler executed his vizier Candarli Halil Pasha.
swap.text: Name this Ottoman sultan whose second reign lasted from 1451 until 1481. His greatest military feat was aided by massive cannons designed by a Hungarian named Orban.
swap.answerHtml: Mehmed II [or Mehmed the Conqueror or Mehmet II or Mehmet the Conqueror or Mahomet II or Mahomet the Conqueror]
swap.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

question.text: After the Turkish nationalists rallied to defeat the Greeks, Armenians, and French, this new treaty replaced, and returned all of the concessions of, Sevres.
question.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

swap.text: After the final dissolution of the Ottoman Empire, this man led the new nation of Turkey starting in 1922.
swap.answerHtml: Mustafa <u>Kemal</u> <u>Ataturk</u> [accept either underlined portion; or Mustafa Kemal <u>Pasha</u>]
swap.clue: This commander had to relocate to another building due to the stench following the seizure of a city in a 1922 campaign against King Constantine.

question.text: In 1845, a holder of this title wrote the treatise "Benefits to Children" describing vaccine efforts for a cowpox outbreak. Holders of this Ottoman title like Enver and Cemal ["jamal"] led a "Young Turk Triumvirate" shadow government until the empire's collapse post-WWI.
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: After the Alhambra Decree, a ruler with this name resettled Sephardic Jews into his empire's city of Salonica.
swap.text: Give this name shared by two Ottoman Sultans, the first of which was captured at the Battle of Ankara.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this name allegedly committed suicide by banging his head against some bars after being forced to live in a cage.

question.text: Timur defeated and captured and this sultan of the Ottoman Turks at 1402's Battle of Ankara. This "Thunderbolt" won the Battles of Kosovo and Nicopolis.
question.clue: This man's reign was followed by a twelve year power struggle known as the Interregnum before the confirmation of Mehmet I as sultan.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Ottoman naval exploits from the golden age.
swap.text: This was Barbarossa's greatest victory, which came at the expense of the Holy League in 1538.

question.leadin: This treaty intended to create a neutral "Zone of Straits" surrounding the Bospohorus and the Dardanelles, and it called for the Malta Tribunals.
question.text: Name this 1920 treaty which proposed divisions of Ottoman lands but was never ratified and replaced with the Treaty of Lausanne.
question.clue: This treaty formalized the territory divisions laid out four months prior at the San Remo Conference, as well the earlier end of hostilities in the Armistice of Mudros.

swap.leadin: At the end of this novel, Gabriel Bagradian is killed while standing over his son's grave, but not before he manages to get his fellow townsmen on a ship.
swap.text: Identify this novel set during the Armenian genocide, in which the Turks attempt to seize the title mountain.
swap.answerHtml: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh [or Die vierzig Tage des Musa Dagh]
swap.answer: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the decline and fall of the Ottoman Empire. Since Chris Ray apparently doesn't know what questions are, your reader will read these statements with a ridiculous and uncalled-for upwards inflection.
question.text: This period of reform introduced many European concepts of nationality to the empire, including the adoption of a national anthem and the creation of citizenship???
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.leadin: Cardinal Julian Cesarini, the legate of Pope Eugene IV, was killed during this battle, but a more important casualty was King Wladyslaw III of Poland.
swap.text: Name this 1444 battle, in which the Ottoman Turks defeated the combined armies of Poland and Hungary, who were attempting to liberate Bulgaria.
swap.clue: This battle began with Franco Talotsi and Michael Szilagyi successfully defending their flanks from attacks by the Akincis and Sipahis.
